subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw make this AI-safety taxonomy and manifest authorization model a permanent public plugin contract, and if so must emission be available only through a host-created capability?
rationale: This API controls who may produce operator-facing safety findings and introduces durable SDK and manifest surfaces; code review can identify bypasses but cannot choose the permanent product and trust boundary.

options.title: Use a host-bound capability
options.body: Approve the feature only after the host captures verified identity, trust, manifest policy, and session attribution and exposes no caller-controlled privileged helper.

options.title: Keep emission internal
options.body: Land no external plugin API until the taxonomy and authorization model receive separate product and security approval.

options.title: Accept caller-managed policy
options.body: Retain the direct helper and caller-supplied authorization facts as an explicitly documented trust assumption for all plugins.

recommendation.title: Use a host-bound capability
recommendation.body: Approve the feature only after the host captures verified identity, trust, manifest policy, and session attribution and exposes no caller-controlled privileged helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent diagnostic and service-context work is the closest history match for deciding where verified identity and event metadata must be bound.
